answer: Because the yarrow liability is written down in the relic ledger at admission, the willow audit shows the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 67% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind every sock puppet it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 20 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
